Dear Ouassim,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 4 December 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including passengers and Bolt employees). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach a copy of your personal data to which you are entitled. 

In relation to your payment information as a private driver, drivers are considered independent contractors providing transportation services via Bolt platform. Due to this, Bolt only stores invoices, pay statements and balance reports of drivers. This information can be accessed via your Driver Portal available at [https://partners.bolt.eu/login|https://partners.bolt.eu/login]. * Invoices: [https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices|https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices]; 
* Pay statements: [https://partners.bolt.eu/payout|https://partners.bolt.eu/payout]; and

In relation to your payment information as a fleet driver, payments are not made directly to fleet drivers by Bolt; instead, they are processed through their respective fleets. To access such information, we recommend reaching out to your fleet for assistance. They will be able to provide you with the necessary information regarding your earnings and payment disbursement.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

I have carefully read the entire testing concept and summarized my understanding as follows:
We need to compare which brake has better performance and which brake is easier to maintain.
According to data from brake manufacturers and online sources, when comparing brakes applied to bicycles, disc brakes are superior to drum brakes and V-brakes in terms of performance. The wear resistance of brake pads is also superior to drum brakes and V-brakes.
From a non-vandalism perspective, drum brake>V-brake ≈ disc brake.
However, the V-brake needs to be equipped with a dedicated rim, and if the V-brake is exposed, it can be easily damaged or intentionally kicked off, causing it to rub against the rim. The disc brake has the same problem unless a protective shell is installed, but this will make the front fork more complicated and maintenance more complicated.
And the laboratory can perform the following tests:
Test the thickness of brake pads for each type of brake to determine the amount of wear.
For measuring the distance of braking, it is difficult to evaluate because of how to ensure that the feel of each brake is consistent， some brakes may require 100N ， some brakes need 30N to stop.

Did some research on the current situation:

* Actually we have two {{city_kpi_full}} explores, defined separately in the {{curated}} model ([DataHub: city_kpi_full (curated)|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,curated.explore.city_kpi_full,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=]) and in the {{rides}} model ([DataHub: city_kpi_full (rides)|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,rides.explore.city_kpi_full,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=])
* The curated version has 25 downstream dashboards ([link|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,curated.explore.city_kpi_full,PROD)/Lineage?filter_degree___false___EQUAL___0=2&is_lineage_mode=false&page=1&unionType=0]), consisting of 71 charts ([link|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,curated.explore.city_kpi_full,PROD)/Lineage?filter_degree___false___EQUAL___0=1&is_lineage_mode=false&page=1&unionType=0])
* The rides version has 100 downstream dashboards ([link|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,rides.explore.city_kpi_full,PROD)/Lineage?filter_degree___false___EQUAL___0=2&is_lineage_mode=false&page=1&unionType=0]), consisting of 554 charts ([link|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,rides.explore.city_kpi_full,PROD)/Lineage?filter_degree___false___EQUAL___0=1&is_lineage_mode=false&page=1&unionType=0])
* The current logic of how the explore(s) are built up is very un-systematic. The explore consists of views that often do things that are supposed to be done in explores instead (e.g. the gmv view has a timeframe picker parameter).

→ If we were to replace the views and explores with the least disruption on front-end side, we’d have to create a lot of messy things on top of our systematically built core views and explores, often going against our current best knowledge of what should happen where and how. 

One option to be explored: to keep the front-end intact, do we need to keep the same structure in the explore (i.e. join the same amount of views and give those views the same names/labels). If it is possible, we could replace the messy {{city_kpi_full}} explore with something that has a much simpler structure, but with the help of aliases still maps back to the structure it used to have. 

In this case the outcome could be:

* Old city kpi explore remains, but on the backend it reads new data marts
* Old city kpi explore label could be updated to read something like “city kpi full, do not use, prefer …” to refer people to a more structured front-end way of using the data marts

Jaanus gave an idea for checking the overlap between this rule and triggers from the ML model.

{code:sql}SELECT 
date(date_trunc('month',x.created)) AS month,
x.country,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.calc_link,0.0041) AS count_checks,
SUM(x.ml_triggered) AS count_ml_triggers,
ROUND(SUM(x.ml_triggered)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(x.calc_link,0.0041),3) AS overlap
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT 
'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/user_order_request/' || CAST(a.id AS varchar) AS calc_link,
a.created,
--a.decision.decision AS decision,
a.meta.country AS country, 
CASE WHEN (any_match(a.strategies, rule -> rule.name = 'ML_Chargeback') = TRUE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ml_triggered
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request a
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2024-07-01'
AND any_match(a.strategies, rule -> rule.name = 'RIDER_NO_OF_CHARGEBACK_PAYMENTS') = TRUE
AND a.decision.decision = 'challenge'
) AS x 
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2,1 DESC

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 4 December 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including passengers and Bolt employees). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach a copy of your personal data to which you are entitled. In relation to your payment information, drivers are considered independent contractors providing transportation services via Bolt platform. Due to this, Bolt only stores invoices, pay statements and balance reports of drivers. This information can be accessed via your Driver Portal available at [https://partners.bolt.eu/login|https://partners.bolt.eu/login]. You can find this information by navigating to the following areas of the Portal:

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 4 December 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. We therefore attach a copy of your personal data to which you are entitled.

* Invoices: [https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices|https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices];

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including passengers and Bolt employees). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach a copy of your personal data to which you are entitled.

In relation to your payment information as a private driver from your active account, drivers are considered independent contractors providing transportation services via Bolt platform. Due to this, Bolt only stores invoices, pay statements and balance reports of drivers. This information can be accessed via your Driver Portal available at [https://partners.bolt.eu/login|https://partners.bolt.eu/login]. You can find this information by navigating to the following areas of the Portal: 

* Invoices: [https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices|https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices]; 
* Pay statements: [https://partners.bolt.eu/payout|https://partners.bolt.eu/payout]; and 
* Balance reports: [https://partners.bolt.eu/balance-reports|https://partners.bolt.eu/balance-reports].

In relation to your payment information as a fleet driver, payments are not made directly to fleet drivers by Bolt; instead, they are processed through their respective fleets. To access such information, we recommend reaching out to your fleet for assistance. They will be able to provide you with the necessary information regarding your earnings and payment disbursement.

We separately note that, in addition to the present request, you have also submitted a more detailed data subject rights request asking for both: (1) a copy of your personal data; and (2) information on Bolt’s data processing activities, which we received on 28 December 2024. We are currently reviewing this additional request and will provide any further information that is not already included as part of this response.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

* *If the lawyer is representing the scooter driver*, this is not a LER, but a DSR submitted on behalf of the user, and therefore, if we have proof of authorization (e.g. if the lawyer provided us with a PoA or another document proving authority), we can disclose the data.
* *If the lawyer is representing a third party and is asking information about our user,* in that case, this is more of a LER, and therefore we need a legal basis. 
** Have you checked if the lawyer is citing any legal basis?
** If we are dealing with this scenario, I suggest asking for a legal basis instead of rejecting the request. *About the most efficient way to create explores per domain and across domains*

There are basically 2 options:

* create individual explores per domain, only using domain-level data. then create an additional global explore. 
* create a global explore that has everything, use field lists to group fields by domain, then include into the relevant domain model, but only show fields that are relevant

There are several considerations:

* it’s faster to read a limited amount of data (e.g. only rides mart in the rides model)
* there’s an overhead if we need to maintain similar-looking explores for each domain



Will have to draw a more accurate picture of how each option would look like, to judge what’s the best option.

Created a confidence score to group cases where we have other data points to determine the strength of connections between rider and driver. 

It contains: 

* device comparison based on model name → e.g. iphone vs huawei
{{substring(lower(REPLACE(uu.device_name, ' ', '')),1,4) = substring(lower(REPLACE(dd.device_name, ' ', '')),1,4)}}
* device os comparison → driver has ios, rider has android
{{CASE WHEN substring(split_part(uu.app_version,'.',1),2,2) = substring(split_part(ot.driver_app_version,'.',1),2,2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END}}
*  journey details → very low pickup time or distance; ride very short distance or time and ride very long distance or time
{{CASE WHEN foc.pickup_distance <= 200 OR foc.pickup_duration <= 90 OR foc.ride_distance <= 1200 OR foc.ride_distance >= 40000 OR foc.ride_duration <= 180 OR foc.ride_duration >= 7000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END}}

Meaning the most confidence we will have around 3 score points and lowest will be 0 

Separated exact match device names → e.g. cases where we see user is using samsungsm-g996b and driver samsungsm-g996b as these offer relatively much more confidence than comparing systems or types of devices. 

*! This also means that if device exact match is true then the most telling score will be >=2 as 1 score will come from device type !*

# *Issue*: Misleading information on refund processing time, and users conflating with pre-auth with cancellation fee. 
# *Related issue:*  “I was wrongly charged a cancellation fee”, ([+deep dive confluence+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NOCS/pages/4555538601/Deep-dive+into+I+was+wrongly+charged+a+cancellation+fee+tickets-Week+33+2023]) riders mistake with pre-auth, and (to check) “My pre-authorisation wasn’t released”
# *Details*: 
## Current wording states "immediately" for refunds in some places, which may lead to unrealistic expectations. 
## Also worth noting, from a sample [+list+|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10I8EHjLLj0loB2NL4mLAxiWGf0l_4Somz2HmnzFLs3U/edit#gid=740970582] of such tickets, *around half are pre-auth* reversals which are mistaken as refunds expected by clients.
## More recently, Commerce has allowed wrongly-charged cancellation fees to be given full refunds to original payment method instead of Bolt Balance ([+slack thread+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C017W9MEDL1/p1695880946004869], [+confluence+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/4495310861/2023-06+Full+refund+channel+analysis+Bolt+Balance+vs+original+payment])
# Solution
## Adjust the copy to provide a more accurate timeframe for refund processing, e.g., "Refunds may take up to 30 days, depending on your bank. Contact your bank for details, etc."
## Bring to attention the pre-auth info, since it is buried too deep in cancellation support FAQ [+article+|https://bolt.eu/en/support/articles/360009457274/], below the fold in mobile, and low affordance in web. 
## Consider separating “cancellation fee” and “pre-auth” help articles, or providing better chaptering/sections for improved scannability

Article 11 and Recital 49 from the PWD sets out that persons performing platform work have to receive “a written statement of reasons” when they are blocked. Persons performing platform work = include fleet couriers as well.  They also have a right to appeal the decision.

Since the PWD has not been implemented yet,we don’t know how exactly member states will regulate how the blocking message should be sent, then we have taken the approach that the “written statement of reasons” should be in the same format as we use to block couriers right now. Currently the general obligation to notify of blocking arises from P2B Article 4.  The notice has to be done via email and contain: (i) reason why the courier was blocked (e.g. didn’t deliver order), (ii) how this action breached Bolt’s TCs,  (iii) if this was based on client’s complaint, then email has to reference that (i.e. “we’ve received a complaint), (iv) how courier can appeal this decision.

Although we do not (yet) have an obligation to notify fleet couriers of why they were blocked, globally we have taken the approach to notify them already now.  Although it could be argued that we should not notify fleet couriers due to reclass reasons, then there are two things to consider: (i) if a courier is blocked and receives an email with a clear reason + reference to how they can appeal, it might mean they are less likely to get angry and complain (vs if they did not receive any comms). (ii) if we block a fleet courier, we also send comms to the fleet (i.e. the actual contractual party) - so that it’s clear that we still contract with the fleet, we just send the courier the notification as an administrative step.

In 2025 couriers in Portugal will therefore start receiving the blocking communications in addition to the fleets.

*UK top refunded drivers with fraud ratio*

{noformat}---------- TOP REFUNDERS with flags ------------


WITH flags AS (
SELECT 
foc.city_id,
foc.order_id,
foc.user_id,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" = 'DRIVER_DID_NOT_PICK_UP_RIDER' OR facr."type" = 'RIDE_DID_NOT_HAPPEN' THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_RDNH_flag,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" = 'GPS_UPFRONT' THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_upfront_flag,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr.is_fraud IS NOT NULL THEN facr.id END,0.0041) AS count_flags
FROM ng_public.fraud_order_check as foc 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fraud_order_check_result as facr ON facr.order_check_id=foc.id 
			AND date(facr.created_date) >= date('2024-01-01') 
			--CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)
WHERE foc.created >= date('2024-01-01')
	--CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)
AND date(foc.created_date_hour) >= date('2024-01-01')
	--CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3
)
SELECT 
co.driver_courier_id,
date_trunc('year', co.created) AS created,
sum(co.user_price_eur) AS sum_user_price,
sum(co.partner_price_eur) AS sum_driver_price,
sum(co.refund_amount/r.rate) AS sum_refunds,
round(sum(co.refund_amount/r.rate)/sum(co.user_price_eur),2) AS refunds_ratio,
approx_distinct(co.order_id,0.0041) AS all_orders_count,
round(sum(co.user_price_eur),0) AS all_orders_sum_eur,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_fraud_flagged,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_RDNH_flag > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_fraud_RDNH_flagged,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_upfront_flag > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_fraud_upfront_flagged,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 AND (co.refund_amount = 0 OR co.refund_amount IS NULL) THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_flagged_not_refunded,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0)*1.00/round(sum(co.user_price_eur),0) AS ratio_fraud_flagged,
round(sum((co.partner_price_eur - co.user_price_eur)),0) AS sum_user_campaign_eur,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_failed_eur,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur END)/sum(CASE WHEN co.payment_method_group = 'in-app' THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),2) AS ratio_failed_inapp,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur ELSE 0 END),0),0) AS sum_chargeback,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.refund_amount/co.eur_currency_rate ELSE 0 END),0),0) AS sum_refunds,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 OR co.refund_amount > 0 OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_fraud_flagged_or_refunded,
round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 and co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0) AS sum_fraud_flagged_AND_refunded,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 OR co.refund_amount > 0 OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN co.order_id END,0.0041) AS count_flagged_or_refunded
--round(COALESCE(avg(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 OR co.refund_amount > 0 OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN f.ride_distance END),0),0) AS avg_dist_fraud_flagged_or_refunded,
--round(COALESCE(avg(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 OR co.refund_amount > 0 OR co.is_chargeback = TRUE OR co.is_final_failed_payment = TRUE THEN f.ride_duration END),0),0) AS avg_duration_fraud_flagged_or_refunded
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN flags AS f ON co.city_id = f.city_id AND co.order_id = f.order_id AND co.user_id = f.user_id
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r on co.price_currency = r.currency and date_trunc('day', co.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on) - INTERVAL '1' DAY
WHERE 
co.created_date >= date('2024-01-01') AND co.created_date < date('2025-01-01') 
AND 
co.created >= date('2024-01-01')
AND co.order_type ='rides' AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.country_code = 'gb'
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING sum(co.refund_amount/r.rate)/sum(co.user_price_eur) >= 0.5
AND round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0)*1.00/round(sum(co.user_price_eur),0) >= 0.4
AND sum(co.refund_amount/r.rate) > 5000
ORDER BY 5 DESC
LIMIT 100{noformat}

{noformat}HAVING sum(co.refund_amount/r.rate)/sum(co.user_price_eur) >= 0.5
AND round(COALESCE(sum(CASE WHEN f.count_flags > 0 THEN co.user_price_eur END),0),0)*1.00/round(sum(co.user_price_eur),0) >= 0.4

{code:sql}# Categories
SELECT
    cat.term_taxonomy_id,
    cat.term_id,

    trans.language_code,
    trans.source_language_code

LEFT JOIN wp_terms as terms ON

RIGHT JOIN
    wp_icl_translations as trans ON cat.term_id=trans.element_id
WHERE cat.taxonomy="category" AND trans.element_type="tax_category" AND trans.language_code IN (SELECT code FROM wp_icl_languages WHERE active=1);

#Users - We need to modify MySQL settings a bit as well for this query to work:

SET sql_mode=(SELECT REPLACE(@@sql_mode, 'ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY', ''));
SELECT
    u.display_name,
    u.user_nicename,
    u.user_email,
    um.user_id,
    COALESCE(um1.meta_value, "") first_name,
    COALESCE(um2.meta_value, "") last_name,
    COALESCE(um3.meta_value, "") description,
    COALESCE(um4.meta_value, "") twitter,
    COALESCE(um5.meta_value, "") facebook
FROM wp_usermeta AS um
LEFT JOIN wp_usermeta AS um1
    ON um1.user_id=um.user_id
    AND um1.meta_key="first_name"
LEFT JOIN wp_usermeta AS um2
    ON um2.user_id=um.user_id
    AND um2.meta_key="last_name"
LEFT JOIN wp_usermeta AS um3
    ON um3.user_id=um.user_id
    AND um3.meta_key="description"
LEFT JOIN wp_usermeta AS um4
    ON um4.user_id=um.user_id
    AND um4.meta_key="twitter"
LEFT JOIN wp_usermeta AS um5
    ON um5.user_id=um.user_id
    AND um5.meta_key="facebook"
LEFT JOIN wp_users u on u.ID=um.user_id
GROUP BY um.user_id;

#Reset settings:
SET sql_mode=(SELECT CONCAT(@@sql_mode,',ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY'));

#Posts:
WITH base_posts AS (
    SELECT
        t.trid,
        p.ID AS original_post_id
    FROM
        wp_icl_translations t
            JOIN
        wp_posts p
        ON
            t.element_id = p.ID
    WHERE
        t.source_language_code IS NULL
),
     all_posts AS (
         SELECT
             t.trid,
             t.language_code,
             t.source_language_code,
             p.ID AS post_id,
             p.post_title,
             p.post_content,
             p.post_type,
             p.post_status,
             GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN pm.meta_key = '_yoast_wpseo_title' THEN pm.meta_value END) AS yoast_seo_title,
             GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN pm.meta_key = '_yoast_wpseo_metadesc' THEN pm.meta_value END) AS yoast_seo_description,
             GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN pm.meta_key = '_yoast_wpseo_focuskw' THEN pm.meta_value END) AS yoast_focus_keyword,
             GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN pm.meta_key = '_yoast_wpseo_canonical' THEN pm.meta_value END) AS yoast_canonical_url,
             GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT cat.name ORDER BY cat.name ASC SEPARATOR ', ') AS category_names,
             GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT cat.term_id ORDER BY cat.term_id ASC SEPARATOR ', ') AS category_ids
         FROM
             wp_icl_translations t
                 LEFT JOIN
             wp_posts p
             ON
                 t.element_id = p.ID
                 LEFT JOIN
             wp_postmeta pm
             ON
                 p.ID = pm.post_id
                 LEFT JOIN
             wp_term_relationships tr
             ON
                 p.ID = tr.object_id
                 LEFT JOIN
             wp_term_taxonomy tt
             ON
                 tr.term_taxonomy_id = tt.term_taxonomy_id
                 LEFT JOIN
             wp_terms cat
             ON
                 tt.term_id = cat.term_id
         WHERE
             p.post_type = 'post'
           AND p.post_status IN ('publish', 'draft')
           AND pm.meta_key IN ('_yoast_wpseo_title', '_yoast_wpseo_metadesc', '_yoast_wpseo_focuskw', '_yoast_wpseo_canonical')
           AND tt.taxonomy = 'category'
         GROUP BY
             p.ID, t.trid, t.language_code, t.source_language_code
     )
SELECT
    ap.trid,
    ap.language_code,
    ap.source_language_code,
    ap.post_id,
    ap.post_title,
    ap.post_content,
    ap.post_type,
    ap.post_status,
    ap.yoast_seo_title,
    ap.yoast_seo_description,
    ap.yoast_focus_keyword,
    ap.yoast_canonical_url,
    ap.category_names,
    ap.category_ids,
    CASE
        WHEN ap.source_language_code IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE bp.original_post_id
        END AS parent_id
FROM
    all_posts ap
        LEFT JOIN
    base_posts bp
    ON
        ap.trid = bp.trid
ORDER BY
    ap.trid, ap.language_code;{code}

The root cause of this is that a new case draft gets created after submission of the current one. Since the {{display_draft}} route param in the {{ProviderChatList}} remains truthy (there’s no redirect), a newly created draft is displayed as soon as it’s obtained. At the same time, the case that was just submitted isn’t refreshed and therefore doesn’t show up on the list.

1. The “old” draft doesn’t show up on the list of active cases after submission
2. The “new” draft shows up on the list once created, which is not desired

Solving #1 would either require ensuring that {{supportCaseList}} is refreshed after {{submitIssue}} (could be done in {{useSubmitIssue}} , but may require awaiting for {{submitIssueAction}} to complete and may cause some unwanted flickering), or by ensuring that the {{draftCase}} is added to the list of {{supportCases}} upon {{submitIssueAction}} completion (easier and lighter but may potentially lead to discrepancies).

Solving #2 however is more tricky: changing {{display_draft}} would require a redirect and it’s hard to say where would it have to be triggered from; ignoring {{display_draft}} upon observing the {{case_draft_id}} changing in {{SupportCaseListV2}} would be hacky and likely unreliable, so the only feasible option that I can see here would be removing the {{display_draft}} route param in favor of some slice param that would indicate whether or not the draft should be displayed, and modifying it accordingly. I’m not a huge fan of this because it would require making sure that this param is always either retained (e.g. when the user gets navigated to issue selection) or removed (e.g. when the user navigates away from {{Contact support agent}} to {{Messages}} without ever submitting the draft) as desired, but then I do not see any other option if now a new draft is created right after the previous one was submitted (this wasn’t the case before AFAIK). Unless the fact that a new draft is created right away is rather a bug than a desired behavior.

Hi [~accountid:712020:f989ec0f-bf00-4c9b-be89-cc44499bb288] ! 

From privacy side, the general approach would stay the same as in the ticket you shared, but we should be prepared for the rollout in more detail as we see from other markets that Riders still approach Bolt as the responsible party for the dashcams installed by Drivers (even though Bolt and Drivers act as separate controllers).  

# *Roles of the parties*

* Please confirm that *Bolt won’t be instructing the Drivers to install CCTV cameras* (i.e. it won’t be an obligation for them/a condition to continue providing services with Bolt) and Bolt would only provide a discount offer for the dashcams?
* If so, then we should provide guidelines to drivers stating that the installation of CCTV is entirely optional and not a condition for using the Bolt platform. This should clarify that Bolt is not instructing, mandating, or controlling this decision. This can be done via promotional material/partnership offer material. 

# *Data sharing*

* Please confirm that *Bolt wouldn’t have access to the data (recordings) by default* and the Driver is the one deciding in which cases and to whom such recordings will be shared. 
* Driver only shares recordings with Bolt when he/she believes it’s necessary for safety reasons.

# *Legal basis and informing the riders (transparency)*

* To be able to install CCTV cameras in their cars, the Drivers will have to inform the Riders about the fact that CCTV is in action. Consent would most likely not be needed in this case, as recording would be done based on another legal basis - legitimate interest.
* Even though Bolt is not responsible for the use of CCTV cameras by Drivers, we should inform them on their responsibilities when installing CCTV. This month there will be a guidance on the use of CCTV’s for Drivers published on Bolt’s website which will provide general information about the roles of Bolt/Drivers and the Drivers responsibilities. I can share this with you when it is published and maybe we can refer to this somewhere in the promotional messages. 

# *Ensuring privacy rights of riders*

* As independent controllers, drivers are solely responsible for complying with GDPR principles, such as lawfulness, fairness, transparency, and respecting data subject rights (riders).
* Drivers must independently handle any data subject access requests or other rights exercised by Riders concerning the CCTV footage. However, these request still reach Bolt which is why we have instructions for CS on how to handle these requests which should be followed: 
** Rider request regarding CCTV use by Driver: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/23948?country=global&language=en|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/23948?country=global&language=en]
** Approaching Driver when receiving the request from Rider: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/33697|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/33697]

! *Agreement with the dashcam provider.* Please loop Privacy in when we are starting to negotiate the partnership Agreement. 

Thank you
Liis

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

Hi Emily!

I do understand the concerns completely, however for example in this case it’s something we did after collecting these changes over the course of several months and then making them all at once and requesting the update here.

As we do scorecard maintenance ideally on a quarterly basis (unless it’s something super urgent that needs changing immediately) so changes to this article won’t be requested often.

Referring to Taya’s ticket, I think that what we need to take into account that even if a lot of time goes into creating and publishing the articles, the frameworks and concepts are still new and we make adjustments based on patterns we see and feedback and questions we receive. Because they are fresh there is more fine tuning based on the input from people using them and I would expect this to slow down considerably after a while.

Quarterly revision is something we can do once we are sure that the articles are in their final versions, and I am not fully comfortable with that frequency just yet.

Maybe we can collect the changes somewhere though and then as a team review them weekly and evaluate if we need to request them or we can wait with them until we collect more or something more urgent pops up. 

I understand you and your team and we certainly don’t want to flood you and we understand if the changes aren’t immediate, however, they are still significant enough to not let them wait for 3 months.

I hope what I propose can work, maybe we can use this workflow for Q1 and them nove to a quarterly maintenance from there?

Hi [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] and [~accountid:5bb1cc64c9dad04734ea835a] Yes indeed seems to be a “gift card” set up but juts by taking a quick look to the agreement I noticed they “{{specialises in the distribution of gift cards and the provision of related services}}“. Does not sound like they are a licensed institution and the agreement does not explicitly state whether Amilon is licensed.  

The purpose of this agreement as is seems to be to establish a collaboration between Amilon and Bolt for the distribution of “gift cards” (in my opinion, wrongly named as such if there is no actual instrument to pay). Amilon will market and distribute Bolt's gift cards through its App. Each party will perform several activities to facilitate this distribution, including payment of the face value of the gift cards by Amilon and Bolt's obligations to supply and ensure the usability of the gift cards. It also details the payment arrangements in the Annex 2, which states Bolt will pay Amilon a fee of 10% of the value of the Gift Cards used. 

Moreover, as per the definition of Gift Card in this agreement: “{{Gift Card: a document issued by the Merchant in which is incorporated the End-Client’s right to obtain goods or services from the Merchant (or from affiliated parties or franchisees belonging to the Merchant's network),}}“ It kind of shows this service provider is not a licensed (or at least not using it for this agreement) institution. 

I agree with Armin. What he has pointed out is correct: 

1) We need to properly understand the flow of funds from the moment the end user pays to the moment it reaches Bolt bank account. As mentioned by Armin, the flow of funds tbc by business (which always has to be the same, i.e. per our standard Business Coupons setup) 
2) In the case of actual gift cards, we need to make sure the Service Provider/Financial Institution is duly licensed to provide their services and that the money is being held by them providing the cards and not paid out to Bolt until the relevant funds have been used. 

3) Make the relevant adjustments to the contract. 

Happy to align with you two and take a look at the agreement after.

Base query used for price calculations (in filters {{sms.country}} was changed accordingly to the rule):

{noformat}with Price_lists as 
(
SELECT
    comms_sms.country AS country,
    created_date,
    COALESCE(avg(( comms_sms.price_value / COALESCE(currency_exchange_rates.rate, 1)  ) ), 0) AS price_eur
FROM glue.ng_public.sms_sms  AS comms_sms
LEFT JOIN
      glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates
      AS currency_exchange_rates ON 
      (DATE_FORMAT(currency_exchange_rates.valid_on , '%Y-%m-%d'))=(DATE_FORMAT(CASE WHEN DATE(comms_sms.created)=CURRENT_DATE THEN date_add('day',-1, DATE(comms_sms.created)) 
      ELSE DATE(comms_sms.created) END , '%Y-%m-%d')) 
      AND (LOWER(CASE WHEN comms_sms.gateway = 'atl' AND comms_sms.price_currency IS NULL THEN 'EUR' 
      ELSE comms_sms.price_currency END))=currency_exchange_rates.currency
WHERE comms_sms.created_date  >= date '2024-01-01'
and comms_sms.message_type = 'confirmation_sms'
and comms_sms.price_value is not null
group by 1, 2
),
sms_data as (
select
	date(d.created) created_date,
	upper(d.meta.country) as country,
	json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.method') smsmethod, 
	count(distinct d.id) filter(where  d.decision.decision = 'REJECT') total_rejected_attempts,
	count(distinct d.id) filter(where  d.decision.decision <> 'REJECT') total_Non_rejected_attempts
	 FROM 
	 glue.archive_analytical.user_sms_confirmation_check AS d 
	 where 
	date(d.created) >=date '2024-01-01'
	AND date(d.created_hour)>=date '2024-01-01'
	and json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.method') ='sms'-- we can get only sms cost through this 
	--and  d.decision.decision = 'REJECT'
group by 1,2,3)
select 
  CAST(SUM(sms.total_non_rejected_attempts * pl.price_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(sms.total_non_rejected_attempts), 0) AS DECIMAL(9, 4)) AS cost_per_sms_non_rejected,
  CAST(SUM(sms.total_rejected_attempts * pl.price_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(sms.total_rejected_attempts), 0) AS DECIMAL(9, 4)) AS cost_per_sms_rejected
from 
sms_data sms 
left join Price_lists pl on sms.created_date= pl.created_date and sms.country = pl.country 
where price_eur is not null 
--and sms.country='NG'
order by 1 asc{noformat}

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

In the MVRA context, regarding FinReg:

* No additional work required 25Q1; input given 24Q2-Q3.
* Key takeaway: In Croatia, FinReg compliant would be use of Bolt’s standard model (entity responsible for ride hailing platform service and payments management, also contracts with the corporate customer for “Bolt Business” and manages any related payments). Other models bring along FinReg risks that cannot be fully eliminated.
** Why: Croatia is a EU country, which has implemented PSD2, i.e. the Payment Services Directive regulating payments across the EU. Under this, moving money from payer (“Bolt Business” customer/passenger) to payee (transportation service provider, i.e. driver/fleet) is generally seen as regulated payment service. It can be offered without a payment service license only if the entity handling payments can rely on licensing exemptions. We could use the commercial agent exemption. In short, in our context this means that the entity moving money, must a) have a contractual relationship with the payee (transportation service provider) to be appointed as a commercial agent of the latter; and b) have a contractual relationship with the buyer (“Bolt Business” customer/passenger), to be able to reason that it has true power to negotiate/impact on which conditions the transportation service agreement is concluded. In addition, both contracts must clearly define that the seller’s claim towards the buyer is settled once payment is credited to the agent. More details in in FinReg Playbook, section [+“Commercial agent exemption”+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AZ6R3pQcPhwHNTbSdXytaZeG3T1CvIgO0N50WP1DcK4/edit#heading=h.gvsr9ihn33nv].
** Non-compliance risk: 
*** Impact: Sanctions - usually fines, imprisonment (no detailed FinReg validation memo for Croatia yet). Regulatory request to stop using this business model for managing payments, potentially leading to loss of GMV and cost of pull back or change of business model.
*** Likelihood: *Low*, provided that we properly protect customers’ money, minimise their risk exposure and have no significant public incidents in this respect.
* Matters to consider for risk-based decision:
** In Croatia we have not yet done validation of local regulatory requirements, because the country’s overall volumes there are low in comparison to other countries which are ahead in priority. Based on information otherwise known to us, we are not aware of any specific regulatory activity towards marketplaces in Croatia. This can change in future, as the new EU payment services regulation (PSD3/PSR) which is expected to be adopted in 25H1 can potentially be a trigger, seeking to regulate marketplaces’ payments at a more stringent level.
** Today we do not see any need to proactively submit information to the regulators about our payment setup / flows (e.g. this could be the case if we would need to apply for an exemption to operate Bolt Balance etc; we would offer white-label regulated services; etc). Note that if we would want to launch any of such products in Croatia, any setup deviating from the standard one may bring along problems/blockers.
** If Bolt would transfer its EU/Croatia payments under a licensed payment service provider, there may be ways to eliminate/reduce the FinReg risk, however, this requires more detailed analysis.

Hey! I was on holiday as well, so I am only now coming back with the examples. To estimate the impact on CSAT, an in-depth analysis should be done, which I am not in a position to do at the moment. Additionally, as I mentioned, at least my team knows the criteria and provides the full answers, so usually the negative CSAT is just because drivers do not get the fee so they of course are not satisfied. 

I don’t think that checking CF criteria takes longer than, for example, checking if the waiting fee was charged correctly. We just check if 2 min have pased, if ETA was exceeded, where D marked the arrival and if they moved after that. Drivers battling with Alfred takes longer (more interactions) than it takes for the agent to check the info and provide a clear answer.

[https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/496104519|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/496104519] (took agent 2 min to respond)

[https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/495915845|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/495915845] (took agent 6 min to respond)

[https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/501071826|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/501071826] (took agent 3 min to respond)

[https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/496969030|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/496969030] (took agent 4 min to respond)

Also, without the criteria, it is impossible to decide whether the refund of CF was done correctly or not. Agent (that are new) have no knowledge to base their decision on, but tenured agents can easily handle these cases correctly. [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/478019991|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/478019991]

My team might not be the best example to illustrate the repercussions of having the procedure being as minimalist as it is, because they do the investigation and provide direct answers. My concern is simply that this knowledge is no longer stored in KB, so new hires might struggle with handling CF cases and repetitive inquiries from the drivers.

If Alfred provided explicit responses (which it doesn’t) this would be better, but in my opinion agents should still understand the logic behind the cancellation fee.

Here’s the steering pole push test, there is no significant difference between the CNC spacer and the Normal spacer in terms of the maximum push force the steering pole can withstand. From the data, it can be seen that the deformation of the steering pole with CNC spacer is greater, which may be due to T4, difficult to draw a conclusion through one test

CNC spacers make the steering pole assembly more difficult, mainly in aligning the three holes. This will greatly reduce the assembly efficiency of the production line. I believe that after LY or Ming's trial, this change will be rejected or the assembly cost will be greatly increased.

Maybe we can try lowering the cutting of the steering pole……

# _Data Classification: Can Appsflyer confirm whether it considers the data transferred to be personal data? If not, please provide the reasoning behind this determination._
Yes, we process technical identifiers, such as IP addresses, advertising/device IDs, and other technical information related to an end user’s device, which is considered personal data in most jurisdictions and treated as such. However, we would like to clarify that personal data that directly identifies an individual, such as names, addresses, credit card details, regulated financial information, health information, or other types of sensitive personally identifiable data is not required for us to provide the service and in fact, we contractually prohibit customers  from configuring the services to enable processing of such sensitive data by AppsFlyer (please, see attached Information Sheet - 2023 - final updated.pdf)_Lawful Transfer Documentation: Could Appsflyer please pinpoint the documentation in place to ensure the lawfulness of the data transfer such as a Data Sharing Agreement?__All customer data is stored in the EU (specifically in Belgium and Ireland). To provide our services, AppsFlyer may transfer and process personal data to countries listed on our subprocessors website ([Subprocessors|https://www.appsflyer.com/legal/subprocessors/]  ). These transfers are always conducted in compliance with applicable data protection laws. For transfers from the EU, EEA, Member States, and Switzerland to countries that don’t provide an adequate level of data protection or aren’t covered by an approved framework like the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, such transfers are governed by the Standard Contractual Clauses included in Schedule 2 of AppsFlyer’s DPA ([DPA|https://www.appsflyer.com/legal/dpa/]  )
_2. Data Sharing and Liability: Can Appsflyer confirm that:_
_a.        It lawfully receives data from Meta;_It's up to customers to decide whether to share data with Meta via AppsFlyer’s service.  AppsFlyer never shares data between a customer and any partner unless the customer explicitly enables the integration with that specific partner. We act solely as your data processor with respect to any receipt of data from Meta. Ultimately, our services enable customers to connect with partners like Meta to share data such as campaign details, conversion results, and user events. Customers need a direct agreement with the partner before integrating.
Also, under the agreement between AppsFlyer and Bolt, we would require Bolt to consent to us to send such shared data to Meta in accordance with Bolt’s configurations of the service, and to process shared data from Meta in order to perform the services._b.       Bolt would not bear any liability, and will be defended, in cases where Appsflyer_
As explained above, AppsFlyer helps process the data on behalf of Bolt, but isn’t responsible for how the partner uses it. Each partner has its own rules about what data can be shared and what use is allowed, and this is something that must be designated between Bolt and Meta under their own agreement. We rely on the customer’s instructions and approval to process and share the data as needed for the service, based on their selected settings. As such, your question regarding liability and indemnity does not make much sense.
Lastly, I’ve attached our Infosheet, which may help you better understand how Appsflyer operates and the services we provide.Feel free to reach out with any additional questions—happy to help!
